sources.claim: frame geometry row, 56 cm (seat tube, angles, head tube, TT, BB drop, chainstay, rake, trail, wheelbase, standover, stack, reach)
sources.value: ST 533; STA 73.3 deg; HT 170; HTA 73.5 deg; TT_eff 560; BB drop 70; CS 410; rake 40; trail 58; WB 983; standover 767; reach 387; stack 577
sources.note: Primary source: Trek Emonda SL frameset geometry chart (H2 fit), 56 cm column, all values in cm on the page and converted to mm.

sources.claim: frame geometry row - independent cross-check (wheelbase, chainstay, front centre, BB drop, angles, rake, trail)
sources.value: WB 983; CS 410; front centre 583; BB drop 70; HTA 73.5 deg; STA 73.3 deg; rake 40; trail 58.7
sources.note: Bike Insights' independently computed 56 cm Emonda SL model agrees with the Trek chart on every handling number, including front centre 583 (Trek does not publish front centre).

sources.claim: stack / reach - second source disagrees by model year
sources.value: 2023 disc frame 56 cm: stack 563, reach 391, head tube 151 (vs 577 / 387 / 170 on the rim-brake frame modelled here)
sources.note: Disagreement is a generation change, not an error. The model uses the rim-brake frame row (stack 577, reach 387, HT 170), which matches the rim-brake / 11-speed / 100-130 mm QR parts spec. Both values recorded.

sources.claim: ETRTO bead seat diameter 622 for 700c; ISO 5775 designation 25-622
sources.note: 700C = ISO 622 mm bead seat diameter. A 25 mm tyre is designated 25-622.

sources.claim: rim widths and depth (aluminium road clincher)
sources.note: DT Swiss PR 1600 SPLINE db 23 published rim data (outer width 24 mm, inner width 20 mm, rim height 23 mm). Same 23 mm section as the rim-brake RR 511; build uses a rim-brake rim of this section.
Conventional 32-spoke wheels are most commonly built cross-3; a handbuilt 32/32 three-cross wheel is the standard road build.
Typical value: 14-gauge (2.0 mm) stainless J-bend spoke, the default for a 32-spoke handbuilt road wheel.

sources.claim: hub over-locknut dimensions and axle diameters
sources.value: OLD 100 front / 130 rear; axle 9 front / 10 rear (quick release)
sources.note: Front hubs are 100 mm, road rear hubs 130 mm; QR hub axles are 9 mm front / 10 mm rear.

sources.value: OLD 100; flange distance 71.6; offset 0; PCD 38/38; flange dia 48.4
sources.note: Shimano HB-R7000 (105 rim brake, QR, 32H/36H). hub_flange_diameter_front = 38 is the spoke-hole PCD; the flange outside diameter is 48.4. Spacing 35.8 = 71.6/2 (symmetric).

sources.value: OLD 130; flange distance 56.9; offset 9.75; PCD 44/45; flange dia 52.8/53.8
sources.note: Shimano FH-R7000 (105, 11-speed, QR, 32H/36H). Drive side = 56.9/2 - 9.75 = 18.7; non-drive = 56.9/2 + 9.75 = 38.2. Flange diameter 44.5 = mean of PCD 44/45 (OD 52.8/53.8).
Shimano 105 FC-R7000 compact, 172.5 mm arm available.

sources.claim: chain pitch, roller diameter, inner width
sources.note: Pitch 1/2 in = 12.7 mm (ANSI #40 / ISO 606 #8); 3/32 in = 2.38 mm inner width for derailleur chains. ANSI #40 nominal roller is 5/16 in (7.94 mm); derailleur chains are drawn at 7.75 mm, the value modelled here.
Shimano CN-HG601-11 is supplied as a 116-link chain; 116 links is the standard length for a 50-34 / 11-32 road drivetrain.
SRAM PG-1170 11-32 (SRAM published cog sizes). The draft list in the brief (...,21,24,...) matches no production cassette; replaced with SRAM's published 11-32 set.

sources.value: 68 mm wide; 34.8 mm thread diameter (1.37 in x 24 tpi); 24 mm spindle
sources.note: English/BSA threaded shell: 1.37 in x 24 tpi ~ 34.8 mm thread diameter, shell bore ~33.7 mm, 68 mm width; 24 mm spindle = Shimano Hollowtech II. Note: the Emonda donor frame uses Trek BB90 (90.5 mm press-fit) - model the shell as BSA 68 per this spec, or switch to BB90 to match the frame exactly.
Shimano 105 FD-R7000-F, braze-on, 2x11.
Shimano 105 RD-R7000, 11-speed, max 34T.
Shimano 105 BR-R7000 dual-pivot, 28C tyre clearance.
Zipp Service Course SL-80, 420 mm, 80 mm reach, 128 mm drop. Some Zipp literature quotes a 125 mm drop for the same bar - 128 mm used.
Zipp Service Course SL stem, 7075 aluminium, +/-6 deg, 100 mm.
Emonda uses an E2 tapered headset, 1-1/8 in top / 1.5 in bottom; the steerer at the stem clamp is 28.6 mm.
Spec value: 27.2 mm round post. The Emonda donor frame uses a Ride Tuned seatmast, so a round 27.2 mm seat tube/seatpost interface must be modelled per this spec.
Selle San Marco Sportive, S1 size: 270 mm length, 143 mm width.

derived.note: Independently reproduced by Bike Insights (583 mm).
Matches Trek's published 58 mm; the published value is used in geometry.trail.
Centre-to-centre distance from seat-tube top to head-tube top (industry convention for an unpublished actual top tube); +/-6 mm depending on where the TT joins the head tube.
Nominal ETRTO diameter; a 25 mm tyre on a 20 mm inner rim measures slightly larger (~675).

derived.formula: distance along the steering axis from head-tube bottom to the axle: t = (stack + rake*cos(HTA) - bb_drop)/sin(HTA) = 540.6 from the head-tube top, minus head_tube_length 170 = 370.6
derived.note: Trek does not publish axle-to-crown; this is the value implied by stack/reach/HTA/rake/wheel position. Consistent with a 370-372 mm road fork.

derived.formula: perpendicular offset of the axle from the steering axis = (front_center - reach)*sin(HTA) + (bb_drop - stack)*cos(HTA) = 44.2
derived.note: Trek's chart does not close exactly: published rake 40 with front centre 583 needs 44.2. Hold wheelbase/chainstay/front centre and use 43-44 mm rake (or keep 40 and accept a 4 mm shorter front centre / 979 mm wheelbase).
Reference for placing the frame relative to the ground plane in CAD.
